newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't confirms offers for 100-year bond.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't confirms offers for 100-year bond.

text.p: Argentina's government confirmed Wednesday it has received offers from international banks to place a 100-year bond in international markets.

"We have had offers from various banks, but we have rejected them because we think that spreads (on outstanding and future Argentine debt) will fall in the future," Carlos Rodriguez, the economy ministry's chief advisor, told journalists.
The business daily El Cronista reported Wednesday that Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers had made offers to place an Argentine 100-year bond issue.
The longest Argentine bonds currently outstanding in the markets have a maturity of 30 years.
